messages.subject: Re: [dynr] Regime Switching
messages.body_plain:
Hi Danilo:
Generally for a regime-switching model with 2 regimes, you have to provide a list of two elements (two vectors, two matrices) to define what goes into the two regimes. This warning message basically detects that in your specification of 'values.observed' (measurement error covariance matrix), only one covariance matrix is defined. When discrepancies like this are detected, the default in dynr is to automatically assume that you want the same specification for both regimes for values.observed and the warning message is just to make you aware of that.
"Oi, Chap! I found 1 regime for 'values.observed' but 2 regimes elsewhere, so I extended the observed covariances to match.
If this is what you wanted, all is sunshine and puppy dogs."

Unfortunately, dynr currently doesn't allow for formula implementation of the measurement functions. It is certainly one of the features we would like to add in the future. Thanks for the suggestion!

Symiin
